title.en: What went wrong in the final?

es: Seguir comentarios que especulan sobre causas y distinguir certeza, probabilidad y duda.

teaching.en: The commentator said the goalkeeper must have been injured, because he did not move.
teaching.es: El comentarista dijo que el portero debió de lesionarse, porque no se movió.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: casi seguro; la pista va tras because.
segments: The commentator said the goalkeeper must have
been injured, because he did not move.
teaching.audioText: The commentator said the goalkeeper must have been injured, because he did not move.

teaching.en: The defence may well have been tired after extra time.
teaching.es: Bien puede que la defensa estuviera cansada tras la prórroga.
teaching.explanationEs: May well have + participio: probable, más fuerte que might.
teaching.audioText: The defence may well have been tired after extra time.

teaching.en: The referee can't have been the cause of our loss, because he was fair all game.
teaching.es: El árbitro no puede haber sido la causa de nuestra derrota, porque fue justo todo el partido.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio: seguro que no fue así.
segments: The referee can't have been the cause of
our loss, because he was fair all game.
teaching.audioText: The referee can't have been the cause of our loss, because he was fair all game.

teaching.en: It might just have been bad luck, so nobody is to blame.
teaching.es: Puede que solo fuera mala suerte, así que nadie tiene la culpa.
teaching.explanationEs: Might just have: posible, pero poco probable; is to blame = tiene la culpa.
segments: It might just have been bad
luck, so nobody is to blame.
teaching.audioText: It might just have been bad luck, so nobody is to blame.

teaching.en: The final was close, so one mistake could have changed the result.
teaching.es: La final estuvo reñida, así que un solo error pudo cambiar el resultado.
teaching.explanationEs: Could have + participio: algo que fue posible.
segments: The final was close, so one
mistake could have changed the result.
teaching.audioText: The final was close, so one mistake could have changed the result.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué causa ve Carlos como casi segura?

choices.text: The heat was too strong.
The other player was better.
Mia was nervous.

feedback.es: Carlos usa «must have been nervous»: casi seguro. El calor lo menciona Sara y Tom descarta que la otra jugadora fuera mejor.

hint.es: Busca must have: es la expresión más segura.

origin.text: After the school tennis final, three fans gave their views on why Mia lost. Carlos: «She must have been nervous. She made three mistakes in the first game.» Sara: «The heat may well have been the cause. It was very hot at noon.» Tom: «The other player can't have been better. Mia beat her last month.»

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué grado de certeza muestra Sara?

choices.text: She thinks the cause is probable.
She is sure of the cause.
She thinks the cause is impossible.

feedback.es: «May well have been» significa bien puede que: probable, pero no seguro. Seguro sería must, e imposible sería can't.

hint.es: May well no significa seguro: significa «bien puede que».

origin.text: After the school tennis final, three fans gave their views on why Mia lost. Carlos: «She must have been nervous. She made three mistakes in the first game.» Sara: «The heat may well have been the cause. It was very hot at noon.» Tom: «The other player can't have been better. Mia beat her last month.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tom cree que el equipo no pudo jugar peor.»

answer.text: Tom thinks the team can't have played worse

feedback.es: Quien opina va primero (Tom thinks) y después la deducción negativa con can't have + participio.

hint.es: Empieza por quien opina y su verbo: Tom thinks…

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué piensa el comentarista sobre el equipo.

choices.text: The speaker thinks the team played well.
The speaker is sure the team played badly.
The speaker is not sure about the match.

feedback.es: «Must have played badly» expresa casi certeza sobre el partido; «bound to be angry» lo completa con el entrenador.

origin.audio: The fans are leaving early. The team must have played badly, and the coach is bound to be angry.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el grado de certeza que muestra.

pairs: It must have been the weather.
It may well have been the weather.
It might have been the weather.
It can't have been the weather.

feedback.es: Must marca casi certeza, may well probabilidad, might una posibilidad dudosa y can't que es imposible.

pairs: It must have been the weather.
It may well have been the weather.
It might have been the weather.
It can't have been the weather.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quizá un jugador se lesionó en la primera parte, porque salió del campo.»

feedback.es: May well + have + participio: el auxiliar have es obligatorio para hablar del pasado.

origin.text: One player may well ___ been hurt in the first half, because he left the field.

prompt.es: Según el informe, ¿qué causa considera segura el entrenador?

choices.text: The field was too wet.
The referee did not see the goal.
The players were nervous.

feedback.es: El entrenador dice que los jugadores «must have been nervous». La lluvia es una posibilidad de un padre y el árbitro es una opinión de un aficionado.

origin.text: Match report: Hill lost 3-0. The coach says his players must have been nervous. A parent thinks the field might have been too wet for fast passes. A fan says the referee can't have seen the first goal.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo presenta quien habla la causa de la derrota.

choices.text: The noise is a possible cause, but nobody is sure.
The noise is definitely the cause.
The noise can't be the cause.

feedback.es: «Nobody is sure» y «might have confused» indican una causa posible, no segura.

origin.audio: It is hard to say why we lost. Nobody is sure, but the noise from the fans might have confused the players.

prompt.es: Completa: «El entrenador seguro que estaba enfadado después de una derrota así.»

feedback.es: Was bound to be + adjetivo expresa que algo era casi seguro.

origin.text: The coach was ___ to be angry after a loss like that.

prompt.es: ¿Quién está más seguro de que el portero se equivocó?

choices.text: Sara
Carlos
Tom

feedback.es: Carlos usa must have been: casi seguro. Sara usa may well, que solo es probable, y Tom lo descarta con can't.

origin.text: Carlos: «It must have been the goalkeeper's mistake.» Sara: «It may well have been the goalkeeper's mistake.» Tom: «It can't have been the goalkeeper's mistake.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué está seguro Tom.

choices.text: The lights were the problem.
The lights were the only problem.
The lights were not the problem.

feedback.es: Tom usa «can't have been»: está seguro de que las luces no fueron el problema. La duda es de Mia.

origin.audio: Mia thinks the lights might have been the problem, but Tom says they can't have been, because they worked well in the first half.

prompt.es: Según Ana, ¿qué es probable sobre los jugadores?

choices.text: They arrived tired.
They arrived late.
They arrived angry.

feedback.es: Ana dice «may well have arrived tired»: es probable que llegaran cansados.

origin.text: Ana: «Our bus broke down on the way, so the players may well have arrived tired.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los aficionados no pueden haber estado contentos después de la final.»

answer.text: The fans can't have been happy after the final

feedback.es: Can't have been + adjetivo expresa que algo es imposible; after the final da el momento.
